items.text: The centroid is the common point of the medians.
The circumcenter is the common point of the perpendicular bisectors and is equidistant from the vertices.
The incenter is the common point of the internal angle bisectors and is equidistant from the three side lines.
The orthocenter is the common point of the altitudes.

runs.text: records orientation: it is positive for counterclockwise vertex order in the usual right-handed coordinate plane.

The circumcenter can be found by solving two equal-distance equations; the orthocenter can be found by intersecting two altitude equations. For a right triangle they are especially simple: the circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse and the orthocenter is the right-angle vertex.

items.text: A unique ordinary triangle and unique circumcenter, incenter, and orthocenter require three noncollinear vertices.
The signed determinant may be zero; then the points are collinear, area is zero, and the usual center constructions are degenerate.
The incenter coordinate formula uses positive side lengths opposite the correspondingly named vertices.
A center may lie outside the triangle: the circumcenter and orthocenter do so for an obtuse triangle.

examples.title: Centers of a right coordinate triangle

items.text: Absolute value gives geometric area but erases orientation; keep the signed determinant when an orientation test is needed.
The centroid is not generally the circumcenter, incenter, or orthocenter; all four coincide only in an equilateral triangle.
Using side weights on the wrong vertices gives the wrong incenter.
